label: sparse conjunctive code: step 2 after "1 z" prefix, and <DEL> step in long sequences starting with i/1/s
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.027% of steps). Activation splits across delimiter step (40% of mass), original-phase steps mostly t=2-3 (46%), and the first 1-2 copy steps (13%). Strong enrichments: prev2_tok=1 (14x), prev_tok=z (12x), out_tok=i (18x), first_tok i or 1 (7-10x), in_tok l/t/s/c/g at the original phase, long L (8-9) for the delimiter cases. But no simple predicate gets usable precision: <DEL> step alone has precision 0.001, and the best conjunction (step 2 right after the prefix "1 z") reaches precision 0.36 with only 12% recall. A disjunction with (<DEL>, first token i, L>=8) gives dev F1 0.12. The feature looks like a sparse code for specific hidden-state combinations of early tokens (first tok i/1, "1 z" / "m z" prefixes) rather than a single readable variable. It never fires at t=0-1 or past recall_idx 2, and does not fire when copying is wrong. Magnitude was not checked beyond the top examples, where the largest activations are at <DEL> in sequences starting with i.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: recall_idx=1 (+4.89), prev_tok=z (+4.19), orig0=i (+3.73), orig1=i (+2.88), orig0=v (+2.82), orig1=x (+2.74). Lower it: prev2_tok=- (-4.19), phase=2 (-3.44), prev2_tok=i (-2.70), t=5 (-2.50).
